seo.title: Homeless help in Denver - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Denver: shelter, meals, health care, benefits, work, identification, and legal support.

page.heading: Denver homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, police, fire, or ambulance: 911 Denver services and shelter guidance: 311 or 720-913-1311 Food, benefits, and local referrals: 211 or 866-760-6489 Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988 Domestic-violence crisis: 303-318-9989, 24 hours
page.notice: Beds, meals, funding, routes, hours, and eligibility can change. Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, benefit, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
page.intro:
Denver uses different shelter access points for men, women, families, and young people. Start with the access point that matches your household. Tell staff your location, age, household members, health or mobility needs, pregnancy, service animal or pet, and whether you need transportation. Ask what to do if no bed is available.
Best first step: visit a city walk-up access point below, or call 311 for current shelter and outreach guidance. Families with children should call the Salvation Army Connection Center. Young people ages 12–24 should contact Urban Peak. Placement depends on current capacity and eligibility.
page.footer: No Home Help is a volunteer-maintained directory, not an emergency service or service provider.

categories.title: Urgent help, outreach, and severe weather

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for immediate violence, fire, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark and describe the danger first.
City of Denver — shelter and emergency guidance

entries.title: Denver 311 and outreach
entries.description:
Phone: 311 inside Denver or 720-913-1311.
Use it for current city-service information, shelter guidance, an outreach request, or connection to the Clinical Homeless Outreach Team for behavioral-health support. Give the person's exact location and immediate needs. Outreach cannot guarantee shelter.
City of Denver — Clinical Homeless Outreach Team

entries.title: Street Engagement Team
entries.description:
Request help: call 311 or 720-913-2000.
Unarmed civilian outreach, wellness checks, de-escalation, and connections to shelter, health, and social services. Call 911 instead when there is an immediate threat to life or safety.
City of Denver — Street Engagement Team

entries.title: Severe-weather shelter updates
entries.description:
Text: send INDOORS to 67283. — sms:67283?body=INDOORS
When dangerous weather is expected, use the normal access points unless the city announces a different plan. Capacity and activation dates change, so check the city notice or call 311.
City of Denver — severe-weather shelter plans

entries.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours.
Support for suicidal thoughts, emotional crisis, or an urgent mental-health or substance-use concern. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger.
988 Lifeline

entries.title: A practical plan for today
entries.description:
1. If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911. For a mental-health or substance-use crisis without immediate physical danger, call or text 988.
2. Use the access point matching your household: Lawrence Street or Crossroads for men, Samaritan House for women, the Connection Center for families, Urban Peak for ages 12–24, or SafeHouse for domestic violence.
3. Ask about transportation and a backup plan if there is no bed. Check severe-weather activation by texting INDOORS to 67283.
4. For food and hygiene today, call 211 or the Food Resource Hotline, then check St. Francis Center, Metro Caring, Gathering Place, or a listed church meal.
5. Use Denver Human Services for benefits, Stout Street Health for care, Denver Workforce Services for work, and Metro Caring or St. Francis Center for ID help.
6. Write down the program, the person you spoke with, the time, the next step, and requested documents. Keep court and benefit deadlines.
If a listing is wrong or has changed: use the contribution link below and include the provider's official source. Do not publish a survivor's confidential address or personal information.

entries.title: City shelter access — start here
entries.description:
Denver's walk-up access points assess needs and may connect people to an available shelter or transportation. Access is divided by household type. A visit or call does not guarantee a bed.
Free HOST circulator: the city publishes a free Monday–Friday bus, generally 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m., connecting major shelter, day-service, and health locations. Ask an access point for the current route.
City of Denver — find shelter

entries.title: Lawrence Street Community Center — men
entries.description:
Phone: 303-294-0157. Published hours: daily, 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
Walk-up shelter connection for men. The city advises arriving before 6:00 p.m. for transportation to shelter. At 2:30 p.m., access opens more broadly to people seeking shelter, dinner, or cold-weather help.
City of Denver — walk-up shelter details

entries.title: Crossroads — men
entries.description:
Phone: 720-305-4640. Published intake: 10:00 a.m. daily, as space allows.
This is a walk-up option and does not provide transportation. Arrive early and keep another shelter plan because entry is not guaranteed.
City of Denver — men's walk-up shelter

entries.title: Samaritan House — women
entries.description:
Phone: 303-294-0241. Published access hours: daily, 4:30 p.m.–7:30 a.m.; the city advises arriving between 4:00 and 4:30 p.m.
Catholic Charities operates this shelter. The city's emergency listing does not state that religious participation is required.
City of Denver — women's walk-up shelter

entries.title: Salvation Army Connection Center — families with children
entries.description:
Phone intake: 303-295-3366.
Published phone hours: Monday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; weekends 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
Call if your household includes a child under 18. Explain the household size, children's ages, pregnancy, medical needs, pets, and whether you have somewhere safe tonight.
City of Denver — family shelter access

entries.title: Urban Peak, The Mothership — ages 12–24
entries.description:
Main phone: 303-974-2900. Shelter waitlist: 303-974-2908 at opening time.
Published access hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; weekends 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. A waitlist call is not a bed reservation.
City of Denver — youth shelter access
entries.address: Address: 1630 S. Acoma Street, Denver, CO 80223

entries.title: The Delores Project — women and transgender people
entries.description:
Bed line: 303-534-5411 at 10:00 a.m.
Beds are assigned by phone only; this is not a walk-up location. The address is not published for drop-in access.
City of Denver — specialty shelter access

entries.title: SafeHouse Denver — confidential domestic-violence shelter
entries.description:
24-hour crisis line: 303-318-9989, in English or Spanish.
Confidential safety planning and emergency shelter for survivors of all genders and their children. The shelter address is not public. Space is limited.
SafeHouse Denver services

entries.title: Food Resource Hotline
entries.description:
Denver: 720-382-2920. Statewide: 855-855-4626. You can also call 211.
Ask for the nearest meal or pantry open today. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask about appointment, ID, address, and household rules.
City of Denver — food assistance

entries.title: Denver Rescue Mission — Lawrence Street Community Center
entries.description:
Phone: 303-297-1815. The provider publishes lunch at 12:00 p.m.; breakfast and dinner are described for shelter guests.
Current provider pages describe public access differently, so call before relying on lunch if you are not staying at the shelter. Denver Rescue Mission is a Christian organization; ask whether a particular program includes religious activity.
Denver Rescue Mission — get help

entries.title: Christ's Body Ministries — Daily Bread
entries.description:
Published service: Monday–Friday, 7:00–9:00 a.m.
Hot breakfast, showers, clean clothing, and hygiene supplies. This is a Christian ministry; check the current schedule before a long trip.
Christ's Body Ministries — Daily Bread

entries.title: Capitol Hill Community Services — Trinity United Methodist Church
entries.description:
Published meal: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 11:45 a.m.–12:15 p.m.
Free community meal hosted inside the church. Check the location page for closures.
Capitol Hill Community Services — meal locations

entries.title: Cathedral Basilica — St. Margaret's Food Pantry
entries.description:
Published weekday service: sandwiches and coffee 8:00–8:30 a.m.; food pantry 1:00–1:30 p.m. Closed on major holidays.
The Cathedral Basilica is Catholic. Its pantry page does not state that worship is required.
Cathedral Basilica — food pantry

entries.title: Christ in the City — Lunch in the Park
entries.description:
Published schedule: every Wednesday and the second Saturday of each month; lunch begins at 12:00 p.m.
This Catholic organization describes an open communal meal and publishes prayer at 1:00 p.m. The provider does not state that prayer is a condition of eating. Outdoor service can change with weather.
Christ in the City — Denver lunch
entries.address: Location: Benedict Fountain Park, East 20th Avenue and Pennsylvania Street

entries.title: St. Clare's Ministries — Tuesday supper and clothing
entries.description:
Published Tuesday schedule: church service 4:00–4:45 p.m.; supper and clothing closet 4:45–6:30 p.m.
The provider does not clearly say whether service attendance is required, so check first if you do not want to participate in worship.
Episcopal Church in Colorado — St. Clare's Ministries
entries.address: Address: Church of St. Peter and St. Mary, 126 W. 2nd Avenue, Denver, CO 80223

entries.title: Metro Caring — free grocery market
entries.description:
Phone: 303-860-7200. Appointments are used for the grocery market.
Published hours: Monday and Wednesday 9:15–11:30 a.m. and 12:45–3:00 p.m.; Tuesday also 6:00–7:30 p.m.; Thursday has daytime hours but closes the first Thursday of each month. Friday–Sunday closed.
The provider states that no ID, documentation, or proof of need is required. Holiday closures and appointment availability change.
Metro Caring services

entries.title: Gathering Place — meals for women, gender-diverse people, and children
entries.description:
Phone: 303-321-4198. Meals and other basic services are available during center hours to the people the center serves.
Gathering Place — general services
entries.address: Address: 1535 N. High Street, Denver, CO 80218

entries.title: Senior Support Services — age 60 and older
entries.description:
Phone: 303-832-1622. Published hours: Monday–Friday 9:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m.; lunch 11:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.
Call about meal availability, enrollment, and accessibility.
City of Denver — day centers

entries.title: 211 Colorado
entries.description:
Call: 211 or 866-760-6489. Text: your ZIP code to 898211. — sms:898211
Confidential, multilingual referrals for meals, pantries, shelter, health care, and benefits. Confirm directly with the provider.
211 Colorado

categories.title: Day centers, showers, laundry, mail, and storage

entries.title: St. Francis Center — day services
entries.description:
Phone: 303-297-1576.
Published center hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 7:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; Wednesday 7:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.; weekends 7:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m. The third Wednesday closes earlier.
Showers, charging, phones, mail, limited storage, limited notary service, clothing in exchange for a cleaning task, ID and birth-certificate help, medical bus fare, family reunification, and referrals. Some services end before closing and are first come, first served.
Mail: anyone may receive mail there, but government photo ID is required to pick it up; mail is held for seven days. Storage: limited to one 30-gallon bag and must be renewed every 30 days.
St. Francis Center — day services

entries.title: Gathering Place
entries.description:
Phone: 303-321-4198.
Published hours: Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Tuesday 8:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m.
For women, transgender and nonbinary people, and children: meals, showers, hygiene, laundry by appointment, phones, mail, a nap room, and computer access. The provider permits service animals, not ordinary pets.
Gathering Place — general services
entries.address: Address: 1535 N. High Street, Denver, CO 80218

entries.title: Lawrence Street Community Center
entries.description:
Phone: 303-294-0157. Published hours: daily, 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
Day access and shelter connection for men, with basic services depending on the day's capacity.
City of Denver — day centers

categories.title: Health, mental health, and substance-use help

entries.title: Stout Street Health Center
entries.description:
Phone: 303-293-2220.
Published hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 7:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; Wednesday 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; weekends closed.
Primary and pediatric care, dental, vision, pharmacy, behavioral and mental health, medication treatment for substance use, and Medicaid help. The provider states that patients are not denied care because they cannot pay; uninsured patients may use a sliding-fee scale.
Colorado Coalition for the Homeless — health locations

entries.title: 48th Avenue Health Center
entries.description:
Phone: 303-293-2220.
Published hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 7:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; Wednesday 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; Saturday 8:00–11:30 a.m. and 12:30–5:30 p.m.; Sunday closed.
Medical and behavioral-health care at the Denver Rescue Mission campus. Call about appointments, walk-ins, medications, cost, and documents.
Colorado Coalition for the Homeless — 48th Avenue Health

entries.title: Clinical Homeless Outreach Team
entries.description:
Request through: 311 or 720-913-1311.
Behavioral-health assessment, crisis intervention, de-escalation, referrals, transportation when appropriate, and warm handoffs. It is not a substitute for 911 during a life-threatening emergency.
City of Denver — Clinical Homeless Outreach Team

entries.title: HOST free circulator
entries.description:
Published service: Monday–Friday, generally 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m.
The free city bus links major shelters, day centers, and health providers. Ask at a shelter access point for the current stop and route.
City of Denver — shelter transportation

entries.title: RTD LiVE discounted fares
entries.description:
RTD phone: 303-299-2382.
LiVE provides a 50% fare discount for qualifying Colorado residents age 20 and older within the income limit. Youth age 19 and under ride free under RTD's youth program. Apply through Colorado PEAK and confirm current eligibility.
RTD — LiVE income-based discount

entries.title: Denver Central Library
entries.description:
Phone: 720-865-1111.
Published hours: Monday–Thursday 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; Friday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; weekends 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Computers, internet, printing, scanning, charging, social-service connections, and naloxone. Ask staff what can be used without a library card or fixed address.
Denver Public Library — Central Library
entries.address: Address: 10 W. 14th Avenue Parkway, Denver, CO 80204

entries.title: Community Technology Center
entries.description:
Phone: 720-865-1706.
Nearly 100 desktop computers with free internet. The first 60-minute session is first come, first served. Ask about printing, scanning, job applications, and device help.
Denver Public Library — Community Technology Center
entries.address: Location: Denver Central Library, 10 W. 14th Avenue Parkway

categories.title: Benefits, housing, rent, and utility help

entries.title: Denver Human Services — Richard T. Castro Center
entries.description:
Phone: 720-944-4347. Published hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; closes at 2:00 p.m. on the third Wednesday; closed on city holidays.
Apply for food, cash, and medical benefits; replace or ask about an EBT card; use self-service equipment; and request referrals. Ask what alternative proof can be used if you lack ID or an address.
Denver Human Services — contact

entries.title: Denver Human Services at St. Francis Center
entries.description:
Published hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 7:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m., closed 12:00–1:00 p.m.; Wednesday 7:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
Benefit information, EBT help, and referrals. Staffing can change, so call 720-944-4347 before relying on this site.
Denver Human Services — neighborhood locations

entries.title: Colorado PEAK
entries.description:
Apply online for food, cash, and health benefits; check a case; upload documents; and report changes. A library or human-services office may help if you need a computer or scanner.
Colorado PEAK

entries.title: Colorado Coalition for the Homeless — housing inquiry
entries.description:
Individual housing inquiries: 303-312-9679.
Ask about assessment and current housing resources. This is not emergency shelter, and an inquiry does not guarantee a voucher, apartment, or placement.
Colorado Coalition for the Homeless — contact

entries.title: Temporary Rent and Utility Assistance
entries.description:
Housing referral line: Colorado Housing Connects, 844-926-6632.
Denver's portal opens only during short application windows and may close when funds are exhausted. Current rules generally require an active eviction or qualifying legal demand document. Check the official page for the next opening and current restrictions. Funding is not guaranteed.
City of Denver — rent and utility help

entries.title: Denver Workforce Services
entries.description:
Phone: 720-337-9675. Published hours: Monday–Thursday 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., except holidays; walk-ins and appointments.
Downtown: Webb Municipal Building, 201 W. Colfax Avenue. Montbello: 4685 Peoria Street, Suite 251. Airport: 8300 Peña Boulevard, Level 4.
Job listings, computers, career counseling, training referrals, résumés, unemployment guidance, job fairs, and employer connections. Services do not guarantee a job.
City of Denver — help for jobseekers

entries.title: St. Francis Center Employment Services
entries.description:
Phone: 303-244-0763.
Published hours: Sunday–Wednesday 8:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; Thursday and Friday 8:00 a.m.–1:30 p.m. Orientation is published for Tuesday and Thursday at 9:00 a.m.
Employment assessment, job-search support, résumés, training, computer access, and employer connections. Ask what documents are helpful and whether orientation is required.
St. Francis Center — employment services

entries.title: SNAP to Success
entries.description:
Phone: 720-944-4347.
Training and employment support for eligible Denver SNAP participants or applicants subject to work requirements and not exempt. Support can include résumés, training, GED or English classes, fees, transportation, clothing, or tools when funding allows.
Denver Human Services — SNAP to Success

entries.title: Denver eviction legal clinic
entries.description:
Published hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
Free legal help for Denver tenants facing eviction. Bring every notice, lease, court paper, payment record, message, and photo. Deadlines can be very short.
City of Denver — eviction help
entries.address: Address: City and County Building, Room 163, 1437 Bannock Street, Denver, CO 80202

entries.title: Colorado Legal Services
entries.description:
Phone: 303-837-1313.
Civil legal help for qualifying low-income residents. Ask about housing, benefits, identification, family safety, debt, tax, or another civil issue. The organization cannot accept every case.
Colorado Legal Services — application information

entries.title: Colorado Poverty Law Project
entries.description:
Phone: 303-532-2641.
Housing legal help for people facing eviction or housing instability. Call promptly and have notices or court documents ready. A call does not guarantee representation.
City of Denver — eviction legal resources

entries.title: Community Economic Defense Project
entries.description:
Phone: 303-838-1200.
Eviction-related support and legal navigation. Contact the program immediately after receiving a demand, summons, court date, or sheriff notice; funding and capacity change.
City of Denver — eviction help contacts

entries.title: Metro Caring — ID and birth-certificate vouchers
entries.description:
Phone: 303-860-7200.
Published access: Colorado ID vouchers on Tuesday; Colorado birth-certificate help Monday–Thursday; DMV2GO on the first Wednesday. Limited, first come, first served, without appointments.
Vouchers cover regular document fees, not driver-license reinstatement costs. Ask what proof is required before joining the line.
Metro Caring — ID vouchers

entries.title: St. Francis Center — ID, birth certificate, mail, and notary help
entries.description:
Phone: 303-297-1576.
Limited help with Colorado identification and birth certificates, mail receipt, and notary services. Photo ID is required to collect mail, so ask staff how to proceed if your ID was lost or stolen.
St. Francis Center — day services

entries.title: Colorado Legal Services — ID Project
entries.description:
Phone: 303-837-1313.
Published applicant hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 8:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; phone applications Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
Legal help for qualifying low-income people, including an ID Project. Eligibility and case-acceptance rules apply.
Colorado Legal Services — get help

categories.title: Women, gender-diverse people, and domestic violence

entries.title: SafeHouse Denver
entries.description:
24-hour crisis line: 303-318-9989.
Confidential safety planning, emergency shelter, and support in English or Spanish for survivors of all genders and their children. The shelter address is confidential. Call 911 for immediate danger.
SafeHouse Denver services

entries.title: Rose Andom Center
entries.description:
Phone: 720-337-4400. Published hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
One location for domestic-violence advocacy, safety planning, legal information, benefits, employment, and housing referrals. It is not an emergency shelter, and no police report is required to ask for help.
City of Denver — domestic-violence assistance

entries.title: Gathering Place
entries.description:
Phone: 303-321-4198.
Day center for women, transgender and nonbinary people, and children, with meals, showers, laundry appointments, rest, mail, phones, and computer access. It is not an overnight shelter.
Gathering Place — contact and hours
entries.address: Address: 1535 N. High Street, Denver, CO 80218

categories.title: Families, youth, older adults, and disability needs

entries.title: Families with children — Connection Center
entries.description:
Phone: 303-295-3366.
Phone intake for households with a child under 18. Tell staff each person's age and any pregnancy, disability, medical, language, transportation, pet, or safety needs. Do not delay a call because you lack papers.
City of Denver — family shelter access

entries.title: Youth and young adults — Urban Peak
entries.description:
Main phone: 303-974-2900. Shelter waitlist: 303-974-2908.
Shelter and day support for ages 12–24. Call at opening for the waitlist and ask about meals, showers, health, education, work, ID, and housing navigation.
City of Denver — youth access
entries.address: Address: 1630 S. Acoma Street, Denver, CO 80223

entries.title: Adults age 60 and older — Senior Support Services
entries.description:
Phone: 303-832-1622.
Day center, lunch, and service navigation for older adults. Ask about mobility access, medications, benefits, housing, transportation, and check-in.
City of Denver — day-center listing

entries.title: Disability, mobility, and medical needs
entries.description:
Tell the shelter access worker about wheelchairs, oxygen, medications needing refrigeration, communication needs, service animals, pregnancy, or a recent hospital discharge. Ask which site can safely meet the need and whether transport is available.
For health care, call Stout Street Health at 303-293-2220. For a life-threatening condition, call 911.
City of Denver — shelter access

entries.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 877-424-3838, free, confidential, and available 24 hours.
Connection to VA homelessness programs, health care, housing, benefits, and local services. Veterans and people calling on a veteran's behalf may use the line. A referral does not guarantee immediate housing.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — call center

entries.title: York Street VA Clinic — Community Resource and Referral Center
entries.description:
Published hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 6:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; Wednesday 6:30 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
Assessment and connection to VA care, housing, benefits, and supportive services. Bring military and ID records if you have them, but call the national line if you lack documents or cannot travel.
VA Eastern Colorado — York Street clinic

entries.title: Service animals at city shelters
entries.description:
The City of Denver states that service animals are allowed at shelters. Tell the access worker about the animal and any space or mobility needs. An emotional-support animal or pet may be treated differently from a trained service animal.
City of Denver — walk-up shelter information

entries.title: Denver Animal Shelter — temporary pet housing
entries.description:
Program coordinator: 720-337-1813. If you need a caseworker: Denver Human Services at 720-944-3666.
For qualifying Denver residents facing domestic violence, hospitalization, treatment, or rehabilitation, temporary care is usually limited to about two weeks. Severe-cold placements may operate below the city's temperature threshold. A caseworker referral, available capacity, and safe animal behavior are required.
Denver Animal Shelter — temporary pet housing

entries.title: Pet food, veterinary care, and pet-friendly resources
entries.description:
The city publishes links for pet food, low-cost or free veterinary care, and limited pet-friendly shelter resources. Availability changes, so call each provider. Do not surrender or abandon an animal based only on an online listing.
City of Denver — pet assistance guide
